claim: Anthropic publishes relative, variable usage limits, not a fixed token/API-dollar entitlement for Pro or Max.
evidence: Max help specifies a per-session multiplier and separate weekly limit; usage help says model, effort, features, and conversation length/complexity affect consumption.

claim: Max 5x and Max 20x are 5x and 20x Pro's per-session allowance; that multiplier does not establish the same weekly ratio.
evidence: The current Max page says per-session allowance, five-hour session reset, and a separate all-model weekly cap.

claim: Team Standard/Premium is 1.25x/6.25x Pro per session, with limits per member.
evidence: Team help distinguishes two seat levels and explicitly states limits are per-member, not an organization-wide pooled quota.

claim: Current usage-based Enterprise includes access but no token allowance; usage is separately billed at API rates with configurable spend limits.
evidence: New single-seat plan charges all usage separately; an individual or organizational spend ceiling can still be configured. Legacy seat-based Standard/Premium retains included allowance until transition.

claim: Fable eligibility differs by plan and its up-to-50% weekly bucket is part of, not in addition to, the regular shared limit.
evidence: The page dated 2026-09-02 grants up to 50% of the regular weekly limit to Max/Team Premium/legacy Enterprise Premium; Pro/Team Standard use credits; current usage-based Enterprise is billed at API rates.

claim: Claude Code weekly limits were temporarily +50%, then became +25% over pre-promotion levels; five-hour limits were unaffected.
evidence: Anthropic's promotion article states May 13–Sep 13 +50%; from Sep 14 +25%; only Claude Code weekly allowance was affected.

claim: One Reddit user measured Max 20x at about 2.2x Max 5x weekly capacity and 4.4x five-hour capacity on the same Opus 5 period.
evidence: Single account, July vs August; transcript ledger and two-minute usage API polling; off-surface use and unknown token weights remain. Weekly reduction estimate after the promo had only two days of post-change readings.

claim: Botfarm reports about $523/wk on Max 5x and $1,100/wk on Max 20x for Opus 4.6 agent work, but those are API-price estimates, not official caps.
evidence: Two short periods from one author's account; lower-bound caveat for untracked interactive use; Max5 arithmetic discrepancy; companion analysis shares author/data lineage.

claim: claude-meter's Max20 estimate is much wider than its HN summary and is explicitly alpha research rather than a true cap reading.
evidence: Repository sample says 11 sessions $35–$401, median $164, one weekly sample ~$1,949; HN summary gives $120–$280/session and $1,300–$1,900/week.

claim: Claude Tuner is the closest discovered Claude app to TiboTattle-style aggregate usage reporting.
evidence: It describes server-collected community statistics by plan and utilization. Current stats page exposed placeholders in this read; homepage's active-user count is a product claim and not an independently verifiable denominator.

claim: Claude Tuner stores usage/plan/reset/organization metadata server-side for synced analytics; ordinary usage collection is stated not to include conversation contents.
evidence: First-party privacy policy enumerates fields/endpoints and treats optional AI Cross-Check history separately.

claim: Claude Tuner's usage-data integrity path changed after it reported possible spoofing of records before sign-in was required.
evidence: The service notice says an extractable shared key allowed records to be submitted under another person's email; new installs must sign in before server storage.

claim: Many popular Claude allowance tools are local-user monitors or estimators, not community allowance datasets.
evidence: Representative repositories disclose direct quota polling or local transcript analysis; no cross-user pool is advertised by these examples.

claim: Historical local log-derived quota estimates can diverge from the account's official usage meter.
evidence: Reddit users report ccusage/readout discrepancies; these are historical user reports and do not independently establish current-version defects.

claim: A Reddit-generated index claimed 23 trackers at one point but is not an exhaustive inventory.
evidence: The index author says it scans GitHub, while commenters identify omissions; use as a discovery lead only.

claim: TiboTattle's Reddit framing was Codex-centric in the reviewed creator post, and a commenter requested Claude support.
evidence: The post discusses Codex local logs and community metadata; this does not substitute for the separately requested homepage-only review in the later provider phase.
